_comment: ioSender's OWN gate cases. The hub's test-gates.ps1 proves the mechanism against a synthetic
fixture and knows nothing about this project; these prove THIS project's rules. Run them with
The testserver cases exist because on 2026-07-21 an unrequested -testserver run sent MDI
commands to the real controller mid-homing. The push cases exist because ioSender once froze a
restated copy of the hub's push rule and silently lost its later widening - 'lets get them
pushed' was denied for weeks. They guard the inherited rule, so a future restatement fails here.
THE 'push mid-turn is blocked' CASE IS GONE (2026-10-29) AND MUST NOT COME BACK AS A DENY.
It expected DENY and had been FAILING since 2026-09-01, when the hub's push deny was deleted for
refusing four legitimate pushes - it keyed off the USER'S PHRASING, which is not a signal about
what is happening. So the case asserted a guard that no longer existed, which is working rule 2's
own shape (prose claiming a check exists is not a check) sitting in our turn config, and the
injected checklist said 'hook-enforced' on its authority. Both corrected together: turn-config.json
now files push under 'NOT HOOKED - IT IS ON YOU', an end-of-session step rather than a block.
The three allow cases BELOW are the live half and are what this file still guards: re-adding a
deny keyed on wording would fail them. If a push deny is ever wanted again it has to key on
something real - turn state, not the user's sentence.
